title: Hybrid priority scorer and eval-gating for model catalog intake
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Customer and internal requests to add new models, pin versions, or request deprecations are arriving from many channels (support tickets, AE asks, platform telemetry). Current triage is manual and inconsistent, causing slow onboarding for enterprise customers, missed regressions on pinned versions, and ad-hoc deprecations that break customer bundles.

Objective: Design and implement a hybrid priority scorer that combines signal weighting (customer ARR, security/compliance flags, latency/cost impact, model maturity, eval pass rate) with an automated eval-gating workflow. The scorer should produce a deterministic intake priority (P0/P1/P2) and recommended path (fast-track, standard onboarding, sandbox-only, require E2E evals). Eval-gating must be pluggable: for high-risk requests require structured evals and human review; for low-risk requests allow fast-track onboarding with post-rollout monitoring.

Key constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Speed vs risk: enterprises need faster SLAs but also higher assurance. We will allow fast-track for customers with enterprise contracts only if an approved safelist applies.
- Operational cost: heavier eval gating increases Research/QA load; introduce sampling-based continuous checks and synthetic prompt sets to reduce full-run eval costs.
- Transparent decisions: provide clear audit trail and rationale in the Console for why a model was pinned/deprecated or blocked.

Scope for this ticket: 1) Define the scoring schema and weights, 2) Implement intake form fields and API, 3) Wire initial gating rules (eval thresholds, safelist, security flags), 4) Produce UI mock for Console triage view and exportable rationale for customers.

Out of scope: full automations for deprecation enforcement (will be follow-up), and platform routing changes for pinned variants (separate infra ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Scoring schema document with weights for at least 8 signals (customer impact, ARR, security compliance, latency delta, cost delta, eval pass rate, model provenance, usage skew) approved by PM, Eng, and Security
A working intake API endpoint that captures the new fields and returns a deterministic priority and recommended path
Eval-gate rules implemented as a configurable rule-set (yaml) with at least three gates: fast-track, standard, gated-review
Console triage mock and clickable prototype showing priority, signals, and audit rationale (Design sign-off)
End-to-end demo: submit a sample 'open-model-v2' intake -> scorer returns P1 and 'gated-review' -> creates review checklist and links to required eval harness
Exportable rationale blob (JSON) that can be attached to customer tickets or support SLAs
comments: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff with Eng (Marco) and Research (Lena). Agreed to prototype scoring in spreadsheet and iterate with AE team.

2026-02-28 — Security raised mandatory flag for models lacking provenance metadata. Added 'provenance' to scoring signals and an automatic blocker when provenance is missing for enterprise fast-track.

2026-03-03 — Design review: suggested a compact Console card that surfaces top-3 signals, last eval snapshot, and a one-click 'escalate to SRE' for infra-cost concerns. (DES-2102 referenced for UI component)

2026-03-05 — Engineering note: initial intake API PR drafted (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4876). Need infra to add audit-log hook and create a dedicated queue for gated-review workitems.

2026-03-08 — PM sync: Decide to use a hybrid numeric score (0-100) then map to priority bands. Marco to own scoring config and rollout plan; Ayesha to draft comms for enterprise customers about pinning SLAs.

2026-03-09 — Research provided a short eval harness (eval-suite/run-model-safety) that can run lightweight regression checks in ~15 minutes for 90% of candidate models. This enables faster gated-review triage for most requests.
